Choosing historical data and compute for quantitative research

Coverage, quality and licensing matter as much as compute specifications for reproducible research.

Research guide4 min readPublished by Surfer Quant
01

Data needs documentation

Useful documentation includes sources, fields, timezone, granularity, coverage, missing-data treatment and update cadence. Samples help verify compatibility with research requirements.

02

Validate research and execution separately

Historical results do not establish future effectiveness or live execution readiness. Out-of-sample testing, version records and operational validation answer different questions.

03

Match infrastructure to the task

Backtesting, model training, data processing and trading terminals require different resources. Describe workloads, data size, operating schedules and support needs to shape an appropriate solution.

This is a general guide to strategy evaluation and operations, not individualized investment advice.
